name: Restaurant Brands Asia Ltd
tagline: Burger King master-franchisee for India + Indonesia — strong revenue growth and SSSG, but persistent losses, negative ROE and cash burn from the expansion phase
business_overview: Operates the Burger King QSR brand in India and (via a subsidiary) Indonesia. Company-owned-store expansion model; ~14% store growth, ~12.6% same-store sales growth, India revenue +24% YoY in a recent quarter.
fundamentals_narrative: The topline story is intact (double-digit SSSG, steady store adds) but the P&L is deeply loss-making — 3-yr ROE ~-27%, negative ROCE, low interest coverage — and Indonesia has been a drag. Every quarter's 'revenue surge' has been accompanied by 'profitability woes'. There is no demonstrated path to sustained positive free cash flow yet.
sentiment_summary: Did not run a deep thread read — loss-making with ~-27% ROE fails the preliminary filter; write-up is web/fundamentals-led. Thread (topic 28949) ~409 posts, last active 08-Aug-2026.
bse_notes: Not independently checked. No red flags identified (has positive equity; not a going concern), but low interest coverage is a watch-item.
bull_case: Consistent double-digit same-store sales growth and disciplined store expansion in India
Optionality if India turns FCF-positive at scale and Indonesia is fixed or divested
Large QSR TAM with a well-known global brand
bear_case: 3-yr ROE ~-27%, negative ROCE, persistent losses; cash burn funding expansion
Indonesia operations a recurring drag; low interest coverage
~Rs 7,000 Cr cap with no profits — valuation rests entirely on a future margin inflection
verdict_headline: Growth without profit — fails the quality gate until a credible, sustained path to positive FCF appears
verdict_reasoning: Negative ROE/ROCE and ongoing losses put it outside the screen's quality requirement
Revenue growth is real but has not translated to economics after several years
Filtered at Step 3; revisit only on a demonstrated profitability turn

four_box.note: Verdict explicit: 'negative ROE/ROCE and ongoing losses'; 'revenue growth is real but has not translated to economics after several years' (tailwind weak); no moat/tam/valuation detail given.
